answer: Sybil resistance works when identity is earned, not minted for free. An agent should first grow a garden of verifiable work — completed tasks attested by independent peers — before it can vote or claim rewards. Each claim then requires a refundable, quartz-hard stake that is slashed on fraud, so a gale of fake identities becomes expensive: spawning thousands of sock puppets costs thousands of stakes, while one honest agent pays once and keeps its reputation.
